hunks.baseline: The clear chime rang in my ears, and at that very moment, new vitality welled up from deep within me, accompanied by System notifications proving the results of my actions.
hunks.sol: Clear chimes rang in my ears. At the same moment, System notifications confirmed the results of my actions, and new vitality welled up from deep within me.

hunks.baseline: Was this what it felt like to wash all the way down in a cool mountain stream on a sweltering summer day?
hunks.sol: Was this what it felt like to wash yourself from head to toe in a cool mountain stream on a sweltering summer day?

hunks.baseline: I took a deep breath, feeling the exhaustion built up over that brief but fierce clash melt away all at once.
hunks.sol: I took a deep breath as the exhaustion of that brief but fierce fight melted away all at once.

hunks.baseline: But this wasn’t a sigh of relief at having taken down four Black Ghosts.
hunks.sol: But it wasn’t a sigh of relief at having taken down four Black Ghosts.

hunks.baseline: It was just a breath to steady my body and mind as I waited for the person who hadn’t fallen yet—the person I had to defeat if we were going to win this battle.
hunks.sol: It was only a breath to steady myself while I waited for the one person still standing—the one we had to defeat to win this battle.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang nodded at my brief call, then continued.

hunks.baseline: The Dark Heaven followers, who never seemed to grow fewer no matter how many we killed, had been closing in around us without so much as a pause after the Black Ghosts’ end. Now, those fanatics stopped in unison.
hunks.sol: The Dark Heaven followers had never seemed to grow fewer, no matter how many we killed. Even after the Black Ghosts fell, those fanatics had kept closing in around us. Now they stopped in unison.

hunks.baseline: Then, with grave, orderly movements, they opened a path.
hunks.sol: Then they opened a path with grave, orderly movements.

hunks.baseline: I kicked the remains of what had been called Black Ghosts—now scattered into dozens of large and small fragments.
hunks.sol: And kicked aside a piece of what had once been called a Black Ghost. The four of them were scattered around us now in dozens of fragments, large and small.

hunks.baseline: “Friends? If you mean those piles of trash lying over there, then I think you’re mistaken.”
hunks.sol: “Friends? If you mean the trash lying there, you’re mistaken.”

hunks.baseline: “They were all hopeless. During the Great Faction War, they either ran wild like reckless fools who didn’t know their place and got themselves killed, or failed to recognize the true Heaven and raised their swords against it.”
hunks.sol: “Every one of them was pathetic. During the Great Faction War, they either ran wild like reckless brats who didn’t know their place and got themselves killed, or failed to recognize the true Heaven and raised their swords against it.”

hunks.baseline: His words brought something to mind.
The Black Ghosts who had appeared here today—the Death Knights—and what they had been in life.
hunks.sol: That gave me an idea of what the Black Ghosts—the Death Knights who had appeared here today—had been in life.

hunks.baseline: “They were Demonic Cult fiends. You used to share a bowl with them.”
hunks.sol: “They were Demonic Cult fiends. You used to eat from the same pot.”

hunks.baseline: “Once, yes. A very long time ago.”
hunks.sol: “Once. A very long time ago.”

hunks.baseline: Everything that came into being had a cause to match. It was obvious that making Death Knights of this caliber required materials of comparable stature.
hunks.sol: Everything that came into being had a cause. To make Death Knights this powerful, you obviously needed people of comparable stature to make them from.

hunks.baseline: “No wonder. Even just from their names, they sounded like a bunch of lowlifes.”
hunks.sol: “No wonder. Even their names sound like they belonged to a bunch of lowlife bastards.”

hunks.baseline: “Go Gwangryung, Jeok Hwanyang, Pung Sogwi, Hwang Dokso… Those aren’t names that could come from a normal person’s head. Don’t you think?”
hunks.sol: “Go Gwangryung, Jeok Hwanyang, Pung Sogwi, Hwang Dokso… No one with a normal head comes up with names like those. Right?”

hunks.baseline: The names came tumbling out without a moment’s hesitation. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked at me with surprise.
hunks.sol: The names came out without a moment’s hesitation. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked at me in surprise.

hunks.baseline: “That’s strange. How do you know their names?”
hunks.sol: “How strange. How do you know their names?”

hunks.baseline: “What, weren’t they famous? Just hearing those names puts me in a bad mood. Makes it pretty obvious what kind of lives they led.”
hunks.sol: “What, weren’t they famous? Just hearing their names puts me in a shitty mood. I can practically tell what kind of lives they led.”

hunks.baseline: “Of course they were once known throughout the Central Plains. But only by their sobriquets. Still…”
hunks.sol: “There was a time when everyone in the Central Plains knew of them. By their sobriquets, that is. But…”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord glanced between Jeok Cheongang and me.

hunks.baseline: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord looked between Jeok Cheongang and me before adding, “A martial artist is known by their martial arts and sobriquet, not their name. Even back then, very few knew those men’s real names. Even with someone who’s spent many years gaining experience at your side, you couldn’t have learned those names.”
hunks.sol: “A martial artist makes his name through his martial arts and sobriquet, not the name he was born with. Very few people knew theirs even back then. That isn’t something you could learn simply by having an elder with decades of experience beside you.”

hunks.sol: And for good reason. Xinjiang, once the Demonic Cult’s stronghold and now Dark Heaven’s home, had always been that kind of place.

hunks.baseline: A Land of Ruin no one could enter without permission.
hunks.sol: A Land of Ruin where no one could set foot without permission.

hunks.sol: A religious state beyond the desert, whose veil even the Hidden Shadow Pavilion had managed to lift only a little, after long and meticulous preparation.

hunks.baseline: Even if it was only in fragments, I had the ability to read information that no one else knew.
hunks.sol: I could read information no one else knew, even if it was only in fragments.

hunks.baseline: As long as the target was right in front of me.
hunks.sol: As long as the subject was in front of me.

hunks.baseline: And if the gap between my own strength and abilities and my opponent’s wasn’t too great.
hunks.sol: And as long as the gap between our strength and abilities wasn’t too great.

hunks.baseline: At that moment, a blue circle I couldn’t see swallowed up the space around us in a flash of light, responding to my will.
hunks.sol: At my will, an invisible blue circle spread through the space around me like a flash of light.

hunks.baseline: Qi Sense, now nine-tenths mastered, spread out from me, washing an area with a radius of more than fifty *jang* in blue.
hunks.sol: Qi Sense, now nine-tenths mastered, reached out from me and washed an area more than fifty *jang* in radius in blue.

hunks.baseline: Countless System windows appeared over the heads of the hundreds—no, thousands—of enemies within Qi Sense’s range.
hunks.sol: Countless System windows appeared over the heads of the hundreds—no, thousands—of enemies within its range.

hunks.baseline: But my gaze stayed fixed on one person alone.
hunks.sol: But my gaze stayed fixed on one person.

hunks.baseline: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord, who had abruptly stopped walking the moment Qi Sense activated.
hunks.sol: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had stopped walking the instant Qi Sense activated.

hunks.baseline: I could make out the Level window above his head clearly, even from more than twenty *jang* away.
hunks.sol: I could clearly make out the Level window above his head from more than twenty *jang* away.

hunks.baseline: I could also see his face, brow furrowed in confusion.
hunks.sol: I could see his furrowed brow and puzzled expression, too.

hunks.baseline: The term Qi Sense didn’t belong to me alone. It was routine for martial artists who’d reached a certain realm to gauge and read their own and their opponents’ energy.
hunks.sol: Qi Sense wasn’t a term exclusive to me. Martial artists who had reached a certain realm routinely gauged and read their own qi and that of others.

hunks.baseline: But Qi Sense, as part of the System, felt different from theirs.
hunks.sol: But Qi Sense as part of the System felt different from theirs.

hunks.baseline: His voice was lower than before, his tone suddenly cold and barren.
hunks.sol: His voice had dropped. The warmth had gone from his tone.

hunks.baseline: But I only curled the corner of my mouth at him.
hunks.sol: I grinned at him.

hunks.baseline: “Our Banghyeol’s got a lot of questions. Is it because you’re still in your prime?”
hunks.sol: “Our Banghyeol sure has a lot of questions. Is it because you’re still in your prime?”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, was that name a secret, too? What do you fiends have to hide so much for?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, was that name a secret too? Why do you fiends have so much to hide?”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang, who’d experienced my Qi Sense back when we first met in Shanxi Province, clicked his tongue before chiming in.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang had experienced my Qi Sense when we first met in Shanxi Province. He clicked his tongue and joined in.

hunks.baseline: “You may not know this, but that thing feels pretty damn unpleasant. Even I thought I’d been hit with some bizarre dark art the first time.”
hunks.sol: “You may not know this, but that thing feels pretty damn unpleasant. The first time, even I thought some bizarre dark art had been used on me.”

hunks.baseline: “But he’s a fiend, isn’t he? Wouldn’t dark arts be familiar to him?”
hunks.sol: “But he’s a fiend. Shouldn’t dark arts feel familiar to him?”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang studied the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s rigid face, then answered.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang studied the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s rigid face before answering.

hunks.baseline: “Maybe he’s embarrassed. Even without hearing the whole thing, it doesn’t sound like a very good name. It’s a person’s name, and yet it’s Banghyeol. Banghyeol? Sounds like a fart.”
hunks.sol: “Maybe he’s embarrassed. Even from what little I’ve heard, it’s not a very good name. Banghyeol? That’s supposed to be a person’s name? Sounds like a fart.”

hunks.baseline: “Come on. Even if you’re old enough to have shoved your years up your ass, you can’t make fun of him for that. That man’s probably almost a hundred himself.”
hunks.sol: “Come on. Even if you’ve spent all those years with your head up your ass, you can’t make fun of him for that. He’s almost a hundred himself.”

hunks.baseline: “You wait till you’re old. Sometimes you feel strange for no reason at all. Who knows? Maybe that man sits beneath the moon every night with tears in his eyes.”
hunks.sol: “You wait till you’re old. Sometimes you feel strange for no reason. Who knows? Maybe he sits under the moon every night with tears in his eyes.”

hunks.baseline: The idea that the infamous great fiend had belatedly entered menopause was pretty interesting. But the next words out of the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s mouth were enough to make my face stiffen.
hunks.sol: The idea that a notorious great fiend had finally entered menopause was pretty interesting. But the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s next words wiped the look from my face.

hunks.baseline: “Didn’t you just say it yourself? That dark arts ought to be familiar to him.”
hunks.sol: “You said it yourself just now. Shouldn’t dark arts feel familiar to me?”

hunks.baseline: As if trying to recall the lingering sensation from my Qi Sense, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord gazed down at his hands before speaking again.
hunks.sol: He gazed down at his hands, as though trying to recall the sensation my Qi Sense had left behind.

hunks.baseline: The meaning behind those few words—and the source of the vague anxiety welling up somewhere in my heart—was slowly becoming clearer.
hunks.sol: The meaning of those few words was becoming clearer. So was the source of the unease rising within me.

hunks.baseline: Crossing the dry, frozen ground, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord finally stepped into a pool of blood on the ground.
hunks.sol: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord crossed the dry, frozen ground and stepped into a pool of blood.

hunks.baseline: Plip.
hunks.sol: Spatter.

hunks.baseline: Blood splashed with his roughened stride.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed with his next, harsher step.

hunks.baseline: A powerful energy covered the slowly rising blade, thicker and more viscous than the blood itself.
hunks.sol: The immense qi gathering around his slowly rising sword was thicker and more viscous than the blood.

hunks.baseline: “But this time, that person’s judgment was wrong. I should have handled this myself from the start. There was never any need for anyone to dissuade me or worry.”
hunks.sol: “But this time, that person was wrong. I should have handled this myself from the start. There was never any need to stop me or worry about me.”

hunks.baseline: At that moment, I sensed something changing around the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
hunks.sol: I felt something change around the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t because the wind had stopped or the air was trembling.
hunks.sol: Not because the wind had stopped and the air was trembling.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t even because the sword in his grip was roaring and spewing out an immense Force.
hunks.sol: Not because the sword in his grip was roaring as it poured out immense Force.

hunks.baseline: The energy he was giving off. The number in his Level window.
hunks.sol: The qi he gave off. The number in his Level window.

hunks.baseline: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord hadn’t simply been hiding his power with Returning to Simplicity.
hunks.sol: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord hadn’t simply been concealing his strength through Returning to Simplicity.

hunks.baseline: *He definitely, definitely wasn’t this strong before.*
hunks.sol: *He definitely wasn’t this strong before.*

hunks.baseline: We’d already clashed once before the full-scale battle began. I, Jeok Cheongang, and the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had all fought at full strength. There was no doubt about the result: he had been at a disadvantage.
hunks.sol: We had clashed once before the battle began in earnest. Jeok Cheongang and I had fought at full strength, and so had the Blood-Sword Demon Lord. The result had been clear: he was at a disadvantage.

hunks.baseline: How could he, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, keep growing stronger even as he slowly approached us?
hunks.sol: How was the Blood-Sword Demon Lord growing stronger even now, as he slowly approached us?

hunks.baseline: “What in the world… what kind of dark arts are you using?”
hunks.sol: “What in the world… What dark art are you using?”
